name: P ZERO Race TLR SL-R

origin.basis: Italian tire maker; Pirelli says the P ZERO Race range is made at its plant in Italy near its Milan headquarters.

positioning: Pirelli's lightest slick tubeless race tire for road racing and time trials, with the LiteCORE casing.
pressure_note: The product page gives no maximum pressure; use the figure printed on the tire.

wet_notes.summary: Pirelli claims the SmartEVO2 compound gives grip and control in dry and wet conditions.

availability.note: Listed in Pirelli's UK catalogue with a dealer finder; sold by retail Tmall shops in mainland China (CNY 737 for 28C or 30C before discounts at one shop on 2026-11-01); North American availability not verified.

price_observations.market: 宝祥丰运动户外专营店 (Tmall retailer)
price_observations.conditions: Retail shop list price before discounts for the boxed 28C option; coupon price CNY 528. Not an official Pirelli store; single or pair not stated.

caveats: A race-day tire: only 28 and 30 mm, with a thin tread.
Hookless compatibility and maximum pressure are not stated.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Coded on 2026-11-04 from a fixed source set: the written reviews on the Sigma Sports and bike-components product pages, read in full through each page's own review list (the newest 15 per page when more exist), every reader comment on Bicycle Rolling Resistance's test pages for this tire, and owner comments in coded Xiaohongshu threads. Counted only owners who describe their own riding; star-only ratings, reviews without riding detail, mounting-only impressions and repeats were left out. Comments on one construction's test page count for that construction unless the owner names the other.

reports.summary: Really fast, much lighter and easier to fit than the TLR RS; the owner accepts a short life for race speed.
Rides very nicely in 28 and 30 mm, but a couple of punctures from small cuts in 200 miles of familiar roads; would still buy again.
A super-fast combination with deep wheels, with impressive speed and grip; a worthy upgrade from the RS.
Very fast on a race bike, with welcome grip on steep descents.
Feels fast and corners really well, but rode very harshly until the owner set pressures well below the maker's calculator.
Three punctures in the first week, all sealed, and another on the rear about three months later; not on a par with the GP5000 S TR.
Three punctures in one 130 km ride and no difference felt from the RS, so the owner went back to it.
One on the front for a few hundred miles; the owner loves it and bought a second.
Four of six 30 mm tires were binned within 500 miles: sealant would not close small holes and plugs failed.
Four punctures in four rides; they sealed, but the owner cannot trust them.
Feels amazing over some hundreds of kilometres, but punctures are hard to self-seal on the thin casing and one needed a plug.
One of the harshest-riding tires the owner has tried, tolerable only below about 55 psi with inserts on wide rims.
